Nov 3 : Arsenal centre back William Saliba returned to first-team training on Tuesday after nearly four months out with a back injury. • The 25-year-old France international has not featured this season after sustaining the injury during the World Cup. • Saliba managed the problem throughout the tournament before being substituted after 30 minutes of France's semi-final defeat by eventual champions Spain and missing the third-place playoff loss to England. • Champions Arsenal have made light of his absence, sitting three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the Premier League after nine matches and unbeaten in the Champions League through three games.

Nov 3 : Supercomputer maker Bull and Schwarz Digits, the technology arm of Lidl-owner Schwarz Group, signed a preliminary agreement on Tuesday to jointly develop AI computing services that would operate entirely under European jurisdiction, a link-up of two companies with big AI bets. Under the agreement, Schwarz Digits will offer the service through its STACKIT business, which rents out computing power and data storage over the internet. Bull, the state-owned French maker of Europe's fastest supercomputers, will handle manufacturing. The two companies plan to design servers filling the data centres together, and could eventually offer business software from Germany’s SAP through the partnership, they said. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. Companies and public bodies using STACKIT will also be able to use Bull’s software for building and running AI applications directly on the service.

Nov 3 : Scotland have recalled midfielder Scott McTominay, defender Kieran Tierney and striker Che Adams for this month's UEFA Nations League fixtures against North Macedonia and Switzerland, the Scottish Football Association said on Tuesday. • McTominay, 29, underwent minor heart surgery in September and missed the last international window. • Tierney and Adams also return from injury, and defender James Penrice, on loan at Rangers from Greek club AEK Athens, has earned a call-up and could make his senior Scotland debut. • Scott McKenna misses out with a back strain. Lennon Miller, Josh Doig, Colby Donovan and James Wilson have been omitted from the squad. • Scotland sit third in Group B1 on four points from four matches, three points behind Slovenia and eight adrift of leaders Switzerland. They host North Macedonia on November 13 before travelling to face Switzerland three days later.

BEIJING, Nov 3 : Guangzhou Automobile Group said on Tuesday its first overseas self-developed battery pack plant started production in Thailand on October 29, marking a key step in localising its EV supply chain overseas. • The facility will complement GAC's existing vehicle manufacturing operations in Thailand, allowing the automaker to localise both vehicle assembly and core battery components, according to a company statement • The plant, operated by battery unit INPOW, is located in Thailand's Chonburi province and will supply battery packs for locally produced Aion Y Plus electric vehicles • Phase one of the project has a planned annual capacity of 7,000 battery packs, while a second phase could raise capacity to 20,000 packs per year, the company said • GAC said the plant would help shorten delivery times, improve supply-chain security in Thailand and support its expansion in the wider Southeast Asian market

SHANGHAI: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met separately with officials from Thailand, Laos and Myanmar on Tuesday (Nov 3), as the world's second largest economy moves to expand relations with its Southeast Asian neighbours. China's support could be particularly valuable for Myanmar, where officials are responding to an ongoing civil war. Wang said that China supported Myanmar's government in achieving political reconciliation and that Thailand and China should boost efforts to tackle gambling and telecommunications fraud, according to statements released by China's foreign ministry. Thailand and China have worked to combat fast-growing networks of illegal call centres along the Thai border with Myanmar and Cambodia, often staffed by trafficked workers, that aim to defraud people in phone and online scams. Myanmar's military-backed government is run by the former general who led a 2021 coup, triggering a civil war that the United Nations estimates has killed 100,000 people and displaced more than 3.5 million.

FAST

Nov 3 : Apple shares tumbled about 4 per cent on Tuesday as its first results under new CEO John Ternus showed that rising memory chip costs were denting the iPhone maker's envied margins, the latest sign of the AI boom's toll on the technology industry. Sales of smartphones, PCs and other electronics have already suffered this year from price hikes driven by soaring memory chip costs as the AI industry's data-center race absorbs supply. That even Apple, long known for its supply-chain prowess, is feeling the squeeze shows virtually no firm is spared. The warning follows Intel's bleak forecast last week on collapsing PC chip demand. "What we’re seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented," Ternus said on his first earnings call as CEO.

"For the December quarter, we expect even higher memory costs. And looking beyond the December quarter, we see the pricing for memory purchases continuing to increase." Gross margin, the share of revenue Apple keeps after production costs, slipped to 47.9 per cent in the September quarter from the June quarter, even with the boost from tariff refunds. The company expects its gross margin to shrink further to between 45 per cent and 46 per cent in the December quarter, as it also grapples with the costs of rolling out an AI-powered Siri that is central to its AI plans. To cushion the blow, Apple has been drawing on memory chips bought earlier at lower prices and has moved to lock in supplies. Its manufacturing purchase obligations, or orders placed with suppliers and contract manufacturers, increased by $33 billion to $89.7 billion as of Sept. 26, a filing showed. TERNUS' PRODUCT BLITZ Apple's drop on Tuesday also weighed on the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq. Expectations were high going into the results because Apple's restraint on AI spending had made it a refuge for investors uneasy about the AI boom's soaring costs, helping its shares gain by more than a fifth so far this year. The memory crunch comes just as Ternus rolls out a product blitz packed with Apple firsts, including its first foldable phone, iPhone Duo, and its first touchscreen MacBooks. Apple has also been raising prices to cushion the hit to profitability. That, along with strong demand for the premium iPhone 18 Pro lineup, helped it beat fourth-quarter sales estimates and forecast upbeat revenue. But some analysts warn that more price hikes risk scaring off buyers as inflation is already climbing. The CEO comments imply "Apple products are going to become even more expensive, which is not ideal at a time when the consumer is feeling the pinch from a higher cost of living," said Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell. Apple is set to lose over $170 billion in market value from its $4.94 trillion valuation, if losses hold. The stock trades at nearly 35 times expected earnings over the next 12 months, compared with 18.23 times for Alphabet and 23.43 times for Microsoft.

Source: Reuters

FAST

Nov 3 : Norway, Denmark and Sweden will refuse to play Russia at the next year's men's Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany due to safety concerns and geopolitical tensions, their national federations said on Tuesday. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled last week to allow Russia to compete in International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) events again, overturning the governing body's decision to exclude Russian teams following Moscow's invasion of Ukraine in 2022. "Norway will – based on the current situation and the information available to us today – not play against Russia at the World Championship in Germany in May 2027," the Norwegian Ice Hockey Federation (NIHF) said in a statement. "The remaining games in the group will be played as scheduled. Our position that Russia should be excluded from all international championships as long as the war in Ukraine continues remains unchanged," the Norwegian association added.

Alongside political concerns, the organisations cited athlete protection as a core reason for the decision, highlighting potential security threats to its squad and coaching staff. "For the sake of the integrity of ice hockey, we cannot see ourselves playing against Russia as things stand. It will end in utter chaos if we do so," Danish Icehockey Union chairman Henrik Bach Nielsen told Danish Media. The Swedish Ice Hockey Association (SIF) also said its team will refuse to face Russia.  "Our stance remains firm, and together with several other countries, we were in agreement that we would announce this decision jointly," said Anders Larsson, chairman of the SIF, adding that it was unthinkable for Russia to participate in international ice hockey as long as the war in Ukraine continues.   Norway, Denmark and Sweden have confirmed they will play their other matches at the tournament. The 90th edition of the men's World Championship will take place from May 13 to 30 in Duesseldorf, Gelsenkirchen and Mannheim. STRONG OPPOSITION TO RUSSIA The CAS ruling sparked fierce opposition from European hockey federations, host cities and sponsors, prompting threats to boycott tournaments, including next year's World Championship and the 2028 World Junior Championship in Finland. The Finnish Ice Hockey Association said on Monday it would use all available means to keep Russia out of international competition. "Our own position is that Finland will not play against Russia," Heikki Hietanen, head of the Finnish Ice Hockey Association, told Finnish broadcaster YLE. Officials in Turku said the city would relinquish hosting duties for the World Junior Championship if Russia is allowed to compete. Commercial partners have also taken action. AJ Products, the Swedish furniture firm that has sponsored the men's World Championship since 1989, announced on Monday it would withdraw its sponsorship of next year's tournament due to Russia's participation. Finnish company Nokian Tyres said it will end its sponsorship of the 2027 World Championships if Russia is permitted to compete, adding that continuing the deal under such conditions would violate its corporate values. The IIHF was not immediately available to comment.

Source: Reuters
